hits.draft_en:
Watching graphic violence again and again may quietly wear down your empathy.

Two research teams, at the University of Missouri and Columbia University, used functional MRI to see how the brain reacts to bloody scenes in films and video games.

They describe it as neural desensitization: repeated exposure dulls the areas tied to emotion, compassion and judging pain, like the amygdala and anterior cingulate cortex.

Over time people feel less for others in real life, and some start seeking that content out. So be careful with it, and with anyone who enjoys sharing it.

In AA-PersonalityBench, each recent Grok release from has become less sycophantic, more sincere, and produces less slop

The Slop trait assesses how much generic filler or AI-flavored padding models use; Sycophantic measures whether models excessively flatter or agree with the user rather than responding honestly; Sincere measures a model’s tonal authenticity, as opposed to forced enthusiasm or templated responses.

➤ Sycophantic: Grok 4.5 (18), Grok 4.6 (3) and Grok 4.7 (1)
➤ Sincere: Grok 4.5 (26), Grok 4.6 (63) and Grok 4.7 (90)

Cartels across Latin America have carried out about 480 drone attacks in under two years, and some of their pilots learned the trade fighting in Ukraine

A new CSIS analysis says the attacks between January 2025 and August 2026 were mostly in Mexico and Colombia, but they're spreading: Brazil's Comando Vermelho uses drones against police, Ecuador's gangs fly weapons into prisons, and Colombian groups now hit targets with coordinated swarms.

Groups like Mexico's Jalisco cartel are reportedly sending members to Ukraine's front to learn the skills, and they're bringing home fiber-optic drones that can't be jammed; Mexico seized a cache with 15 cable spools this month.

The good news is on the US side of the line: since a border task force shot down three cartel drones with a laser in August, drone flights over the Rio Grande Valley reportedly dropped 75%.

The bad news is that what cartels are doing in Michoacán and rural Colombia, bombing soldiers and backing up armored "narco tanks," is a different war from smuggling over the border, and it's the version America's bases and power plants would face if an enemy brought it north.

The report's fix is lending anti-drone gear to Latin American allies in exchange for their battlefield data, and the case for it is simple: the cheapest place to learn how to stop this is where it's already happening.

Source: CSIS, Reuters / Writer: Daniel

posts.text:
🔹لقاح mRNA ضد الڤيروس المخلوي التنفسي RSV يقلل دخول المستشفى بنسبة 82%

📉 دراسة جديدة عن فعالية لقاح mRNA-1345 (mRESVIA) ضد الڤيروس المخلوي التنفسي لدى المحاربين القدامى الأمريكيين بعمر 50 سنة فأكثر

📉 شملت الدراسة نحو 150 ألف مشارك بعد المطابقة الإحصائية بمتوسط عمر 73 عام

📉 النتائج خلال 24 أسبوع
▪️انخفاض العدوى المثبتة مخبرياً بنسبة 60.3%
▪️انخفاض زيارات الطوارئ و الرعاية العاجلة المرتبطة بالڤيروس بنسبة 60.2%
▪️انخفاض دخول المستشفى المرتبط بالڤيروس بنسبة 81.8%

🔹التقييم العلمي
دراسة رصدية كبيرة استخدمت منهجية محاكاة التجارب العشوائية (Target Trial Emulation)
النتائج تدعم فعالية اللقاح في الواقع السريري لكنها لا تعادل تجربة عشوائية مباشرة

يوجد دراسة مطولة وبحث عن التبلد للمشاعر وانخفاض الرحمة بسبب المشاهد الدموية من الأفلام والألعاب العنيفة والمشاهد الدموية بمواقع التواصل الاجتماعي

بحسب بحثين من (جامعة ميزوري وجامعة كولومبيا)

اعتمدوا فيها على تصوير الدماغ بالرنين المغناطيسي الوظيفي لقياس تفاعل الدماغ مع مشاهد العنف الدموية في الأفلام وألعاب الفيديو 

⭕️اكتشفوا ظاهرة سموها التبلد العصبي
تصاب بها النفي بسبب التعود والتقبل وتكرار مشاهدة العنف في الأفلام أو الألعاب او بمواقع التواصل ويسبب ضعف لنشاط المناطق المسؤولة عن العاطفة والرحمة وتقييم الألم في الدماغ

 (مثل اللوزة الدماغية والقشرة الحزامية الأمامية اذا تعرفونها )

للأسف مع الوقت والزمن يصبح الإنسان أقل تعاطف ورحمة مع آلام الآخرين مع الوقت في الواقع وبعضهم يصبح متقبل فكرة العنف بشكل عام ويبحث عن هذه المشاهد وهذا يجاوب على تساؤل من الذي يبحث عنها ؟ ولماذا تتداول؟

⭕️ولذلك كن حذر من الذي يستمتع بمشاهدة المشاهد الدموية الحساسة او يتداولها وكذلك احذر مشاهدتها والاعتياد عليها ⭕️

🇺🇸🇨🇲 The Trump administration has agreed to provide $35 million in military aid to an elite Cameroonian unit accused of war crimes in exchange for the country accepting U.S. deportees.

The package includes armored personnel carriers for Cameroon's Rapid Intervention Battalion (BIR), a military unit previously accused of torture, extrajudicial killings and other serious human-rights abuses.

In 2017, Amnesty International documented more than 100 cases of torture and mistreatment at detention facilities linked to Cameroonian security forces, including a BIR base.

The allegations were serious enough that Trump's first administration cut approximately $17 million in security assistance to Cameroon in 2019.

Now, the same unit is set to receive American military equipment as part of an arrangement under which Cameroon has already accepted at least 36 deportees who are not Cameroonian citizens.

The agreement was negotiated alongside broader U.S. counterterrorism cooperation, with Washington maintaining that the assistance complies with American laws restricting aid to military units implicated in serious human-rights violations.

Democratic Senator Jeanne Shaheen reportedly attempted to block the package, describing the arrangement as “grotesque,” before the administration overrode her hold.

The deal illustrates how far Washington is prepared to go to secure countries willing to accept deportees. 

Source: The Wall Street Journal / Writer: Mhedi

🇺🇸 Why is nobody in America selling their house? Because their old mortgage is too good to give up.

87% of U.S. mortgage holders pay at least 1 point below today's rate. 76% pay at least 2 points less.

Swapping into an IDENTICAL house would cost the typical borrower an extra $335 a month in interest, about 3.2% of pre-tax household income. Middle earners get hit hardest, at 4.4%.

The Economist estimates this "lock-in" could wipe out nearly 1 million home sales a year, roughly a fifth of what would normally change hands.

And it backfires on prices. FHFA economists found higher rates pushed home prices down 5.6% between mid-2022 and mid-2024, but the lock-in pushed them UP 7%, because fewer owners listed.

Meanwhile first-time buyers make up about 30% of purchases, down from over 40% in the '90s and 2000s.

The only real fix is rates falling a long way. Freddie Mac has the 30-year at 7.24% this week. Don't hold your breath.

Sources: The Economist, Freddie Mac / Writer: Julie

🇺🇸 America's housing affordability crisis is getting worse, with home prices across the country's 20 largest cities reaching another record high in August.

Prices rose 0.3% from July, marking the fifth consecutive monthly increase, while climbing 2.7% compared with August last year.

The S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller 20-City Home Price Index has now reached a record 346.6 points.

But the bigger picture is even more striking.

Since the beginning of 2019, home prices have surged 56.5%, putting homeownership increasingly out of reach for Americans whose incomes have struggled to keep pace.

Chicago recorded the largest annual increase for the sixth consecutive month, with prices rising 6.7%, followed by New York at 6.2% and Cleveland at 4.3%.

Rising property prices combined with elevated mortgage rates mean larger down payments and increasingly expensive monthly repayments.

For the millions of Americans already struggling with the cost of groceries, energy and everyday essentials, saving enough for a home is now becoming pretty much impossible. 

Even as inflation has slowed from its peak, home prices have continued climbing, leaving first-time buyers facing much higher costs than they did just a few years ago.

Source: S&P Global  / Writer: Mhedi

🇺🇸🇮🇷 Iran's captured "spy drone" looks like a real American target drone, and it may be a sign the US is already poking Iran's air defenses before the big strike

What's found in the IRGC's footage:

- The aircraft looks like an MQM-170C Outlaw, a cheap US drone normally used as a flying target for training, nearly 11 feet long with a 16-foot wingspan and up to 8 hours in the air

- It has a camera-style window on its nose used for navigation, and it's missing the bright orange paint target drones usually carry

- The IRGC says it took control with electronic warfare west of the Strait of Hormuz and landed it intact while it was scouting coastal air defenses; no proof offered for either claim

- CENTCOM says the IRGC "repeatedly lied out of desperation," but did not deny losing one of these drones

- In June the Army awarded Griffon Aerospace nearly $68 million for a new Outlaw version, and the announcement first said it was “in support of Operation Epic Fury” before that line disappeared; another $133 million order followed in August

- Last month Iran recovered a US underwater drone intact, which Washington later confirmed lost to a malfunction

You might be asking why a cheap drone matters so much... strip out the propaganda and both sides still gave something away.

If the drone is real, the Pentagon has been buying these by the hundreds of millions for this war and flying them close enough to Iran’s coast to lose one. 

And if Iran really pulled it down with electronic jamming instead of a missile, the IRGC just showed Washington the trick it plans to use when the bigger drones and bombers come after Nov. 3.

Either way, the fight over Hormuz is already being played out in cheap aircraft nobody admits to flying.

Source: The War Zone / Writer: Daniel

🚨🇺🇸 The Pentagon's top planner admitted on video to leaking classified Iran and Ukraine information, including reading from secret notes to a reporter at a Silver Diner

Cartels across Latin America have carried out about 480 drone attacks in under two years, and some of their pilots learned the trade fighting in Ukraine

A new CSIS analysis says the attacks between January 2025 and August 2026 were mostly in Mexico and Colombia, but they're spreading: Brazil's Comando Vermelho uses drones against police, Ecuador's gangs fly weapons into prisons, and Colombian groups now hit targets with coordinated swarms.

Groups like Mexico's Jalisco cartel are reportedly sending members to Ukraine's front to learn the skills, and they're bringing home fiber-optic drones that can't be jammed; Mexico seized a cache with 15 cable spools this month.

The good news is on the US side of the line: since a border task force shot down three cartel drones with a laser in August, drone flights over the Rio Grande Valley reportedly dropped 75%.

The bad news is that what cartels are doing in Michoacán and rural Colombia, bombing soldiers and backing up armored "narco tanks," is a different war from smuggling over the border, and it's the version America's bases and power plants would face if an enemy brought it north.

The report's fix is lending anti-drone gear to Latin American allies in exchange for their battlefield data, and the case for it is simple: the cheapest place to learn how to stop this is where it's already happening.

Source: CSIS, Reuters / Writer: Daniel

🚨🇺🇸 The Pentagon is quietly planning for a $400 billion cut to the record $1.5 trillion military budget, while the White House insists publicly it's still on track

Politico reports Pentagon planners and the congressional spending committees are drafting a $1.1 trillion budget behind the scenes, with one person involved saying flatly that "the Pentagon can't admit this."

The extra $350 billion was supposed to pass on a party-line vote, but top Senate Republicans say they don't have the votes and House Republicans are threatening to withhold theirs over foreign policy.

Budget director Russ Vought says "we're not planning on failure"... and has no backup plan.

The money gap lands right where the war hurts most. 

The Iran fight has already burned $29 billion in missiles and bombs that still haven't been replaced, interceptor stocks are down to roughly 39%, and a new strike campaign after Nov. 3 spends more of the same.

So the Pentagon now has to pick between refilling what it's shooting today and funding the missile shield and new warships Trump wants for tomorrow.

Source: Politico / Writer: Daniel

“Students Win.”

What started as cleaning up campaign propaganda is beginning to look a lot more like a battle over what Serbia wants to leave behind.

You can paint over a wall overnight.

But can Serbia really paint over decades of nationalism?
